g_roast: Sixteen years of school groups at the snake house, mates, and none of them ever wandered off as fast as you lot.
I've handled taipans with better judgement than this party. And the taipans were having a bad day.
g_fire_back: Fair call, from the bloke who screamed at a gecko this morning. A gecko, mate.
Careful, mate, my sister's a lawyer, and she taught me every comeback she ever used in court.
g_pile_on: And then they tried to cook on a fire that wasn't lit. Waited twenty minutes, mate, patient as anything.
Oh, it gets better, I was watching. They tried to pat the scorpion, and the scorpion had opinions.
lines.g_peacemake: Easy, easy, both of you. My mum ran a childcare centre, and I've seen four-year-olds settle this faster. Sit, grab a cold one, and breathe.
lines.g_take_side: Sorry, mate, I'm with this one. My sister would argue it in court and win before lunch.
lines.g_left_out: You two have a proper chat going, no worries. I'll find something to do with my hands.
lines.g_include: Come and sit down, there's heaps of room. Nobody stands around at a Brisbane barbie, it's practically illegal.
lines.g_bad_plan: Right, here's my plan. We walk in, I pick up the biggest thing in there, and we all hope it's in a good mood.
lines.g_plan_yes: Yeah, nice, calm and simple, my favourite kind of plan. Count me in, mate.
lines.g_plan_no: Nah, mate, that plan corners something frightened. A cornered animal bites, and so does this plan.
lines.g_hype: Righto, mates, slow and calm, no sudden moves. Let's say hello to whatever's down there.
lines.g_toast: Short one, I've got a beer to get to. To you lot, the best company I've had that wasn't cold-blooded.
lines.g_cheers: Cheers, mates, bottoms up, and somebody check that mug for spiders first.
g_quiet_line: There's a nest of something under that rock, by the way. Leave it, it's not bothering anyone.
Reckon the Broncos would've won the grand final by now, if there's still footy back home. Somebody tell me there's still footy.
lines.g_after_wipe: No worries, no worries, everyone up, slowly. Breathe, have some water, and then we sort out where it went sideways.
lines.g_crew: I've always been easier around animals than people, mates. Turns out you lot are almost as interesting as a snake, and you tell better jokes.
lines.g_exasperated: Calm and quiet, that was the whole plan, mates, two words. You lot turned it into a stampede in about four seconds.
lines.g_love_sharp: You read a creature before it moves, mate. Took me ten years at the sanctuary to learn that.
lines.g_love_kind: You're gentle with frightened people, mate. My mum's like that with the little ones at her centre.
lines.g_love_funny: You make me laugh, and I spend most days laughing at near-death experiences. High bar, mate.
lines.g_love_brave: You walk straight up to trouble without a flinch. Takes guts, and I've got a lot of time for guts.
lines.g_love_steady: Your heart rate never seems to go up, mate. I wish I could bottle it for my mum, she worries about everything.
lines.g_love_clever: You work out why a thing happens, not just what happened. My dad was like that with wiring, and I always envied it.
lines.g_love_honest: You tell people the true thing, no fluff. My sister does that for a living, and you do it for free.
lines.g_love_quiet: You don't spook anything, you just sit there calm and quiet. I'd hire you at the snake house tomorrow.
lines.g_love_fierce: You hang on like a croc on a death roll, and I mean that as the highest praise.
lines.g_love_warm: Hanging around you is like a Sunday arvo barbie in Brisbane, everyone mellow. Didn't know I missed it.
g_loved: Ah, mate, that's lovely, I'm going a bit red. Must be the sun.
No worries, and thanks, really. Don't tell the scorpion, she gets jealous.
lines.g_hate_sharp: You go for the soft bit every time, like a dingo after a lamb. Nobody's impressed, mate.
lines.g_hate_kind: Stop checking on me after every scratch, mate. My mum did that for twenty years, and I turned out fine.
lines.g_hate_funny: There's a time for jokes, mate, and it's not when somebody's hurt and scared.
lines.g_hate_brave: You charge at everything like it owes you money. That's how people get hurt, and then they blame the wrong thing.
lines.g_hate_steady: You hang back so long the moment walks off without you. Sometimes you just have a go, mate.
lines.g_hate_clever: You lecture me about venom like I haven't had it in my veins. I've literally had it in my veins.
lines.g_hate_honest: Everything you think falls straight out. Even a blue-tongue keeps its mouth shut some of the time.
lines.g_hate_quiet: You never let on what's wrong, then you're cranky about it. Even my sister tells me when I've stuffed up, and loudly.
lines.g_hate_fierce: Everything's a fight with you, like a pair of goannas over a dead roo. Ease up a bit.
lines.g_hate_warm: Mate, you talk the ears off everyone. Even my sister would struggle to get a word in, and she bills by the hour.
lines.g_respect: We don't really get on, mate, and that's fine. But you didn't flinch back there, and I respect a steady hand.
lines.g_call_out: That one was on you, mate. I said slow and calm, and you went loud and fast, and look what it did.
lines.g_stung: Yeah, alright, message received. I'll go cool off by myself for a bit.
lines.g_concede: You had the right read back there, and I didn't. Stewed on it all day, and you were spot on.
lines.g_nod: Not bad yourself, mate. Let's not make a fuss about it.
lines.g_callback_save: Haven't forgotten you pulling me out of that one. Usually it's me pulling things out of holes, makes a nice change.
lines.g_callback_clutch: You and me, last two on our feet, bleeding a bit and grinning like idiots. Best day out I've had in years.
lines.g_callback_callout: When you had a go at me that time, I sulked under a rock like a cranky skink. You were right though.
lines.g_former_rivals: First week, I had you pegged as a stick-poker. These days I'd hand you the hook and go in first.
lines.g_changed: I used to only talk to the animals, mates. Now look at me, yarning with you lot till midnight.
g_unguarded: Since it's quiet, then. My first eighteen months here, I poisoned myself on purpose, alone, and wrote it down badly. It worked, though, mostly.
Every girlfriend I ever had left because the house was full of tanks. Can't say I blame them, mate, it was a lot of tanks.
lines.g_clipped: Yeah, no worries, whatever. I'll be over by the rocks.
lines.g_noticed_open: Look at that, the quiet one's talking, full sentences and everything. Don't stop, mate, I'm enjoying this.
arg_ask: {player}, mate, can you sort this out? I've said my piece, and they're not having it.
You be the ranger on this one, {player}. Whatever you say goes, fair?
lines.arg_backed_me: Good on ya, {player}, knew you'd see it.
lines.arg_backed_them: Fair enough, you're the boss, no worries. I reckon you're wrong, but no worries.
lines.arg_stayed_out: Not getting involved, eh? Sensible, like a possum in a high tree.
lines.arg_always_their_side: Always them, {player}, every single argument. I'm laid back, mate, not asleep.
lines.arg_wallflower: Nobody wants to call it, so I will, mate. I'm right, and we're moving on.
lines.arg_reject: Nah, {player}, mate, not that one. That ends with somebody hurt and somebody blaming the snake.
lines.arg_grumble: My money's still on me being right, mate. Not going to bang on about it.
lines.arg_settled: Call it a draw, mate, fifty-fifty. Shake on it and grab a beer.
lines.seen_listens: You wait out people's whole yarn, {player}. School kids never managed that, and neither did my sister.
lines.seen_truth: You give it to people straight, {player}, no sugar on it. Animals respect that, and so do I.
lines.seen_jokes: The moment things turn ugly, out comes a joke, {player}. My dad did that during storms, kept the whole house calm.
lines.seen_stays_out: You don't buy into other people's barneys, {player}. Smart, mate, like a lizard staying under its rock.
lines.seen_biased: First pick of the gear goes the same way every trip, {player}. Even the scorpion's noticed, and she's not observant.
lines.seen_harsh: You can be a bit harsh on folks, {player}. I've got thick skin from the bites, but not everyone has.
lines.seed_right: Your advice after that mess of a fight, {player}, didn't love it. Did it your way today and nobody got bitten.
lines.seed_remember: Still mulling over your words from that bad day. Haven't made my mind up yet, mate.
lines.seed_wrong: Gave your way a go, {player}, and it went worse. Just letting you know, no dramas.
lines.talk_aftermath_near_death: Can I grab you for a sec, {player}? That one got nearer than I'd let on, and I don't rattle easy.
lines.talk_aftermath_wipe: We all went down, the whole lot of us. Sit with me, and we'll go through it like a bad handling, move by move.
lines.talk_aftermath_blame_self: {name} copped it first, and reading creatures is the one thing I'm meant to be good at. I missed the warning, {player}.
lines.talk_aftermath_first_clear: In and out, nobody bitten, nobody hurt. At the sanctuary that'd be a perfect show, mate.
lines.talk_development: Odd one, {player}, bear with me. Reckon I've changed? I keep choosing the campfire over a quiet rock, and that's not like me.
lines.talk_relationship_hard_on: I've been a bit sharp with {name}. I talk to people like they're handlers, and they're not handlers.
lines.talk_relationship_likes_me: Give me the honest version, {player}. Is {name} fond of me, or just putting up with the scorpion bloke?
lines.talk_relationship_respect_hate: {name} gets right up my nose, {player}. But in a nest of something nasty, I'd want them holding the light.
lines.talk_relationship_acting_off: {name}'s gone a bit flighty, {player}, like an animal that's hurt and hiding it. Worth a look, I reckon.
lines.talk_confrontation_favour: Quick one, {player}, said nicely. Every decent bit of gear ends up in {name}'s tank, and everyone's noticed.
lines.talk_confrontation_dislike: Might as well be upfront, mate. Me and {name} are a mongoose and a cobra, and there's no point dressing it up.
lines.talk_confrontation_risks: We keep reaching into holes without looking, {player}. I've got the scars, mate, and I'd like a few less new ones.
lines.talk_confrontation_wrong: I misread {name}, {player}, proper misread. They had it right, and I'd rather own that now than later.
lines.talk_confrontation_trust: Can I ask you something blunt, {player}? On the hard runs, I'm left minding camp. Is that tactics, or do you reckon I'm not up to it?
lines.talk_confrontation_decided: My gear wandered off to {name}, no word to me at all. One quick ask and it was theirs, {player}, happily.
lines.talk_shrug_aftermath: I'll be right, mate, I always am. Takes more than that.
lines.talk_stings_aftermath: Not what I needed, mate, honestly not. I'll go sit with the scorpion.
lines.talk_lands_development: Yeah, you've noticed too. Good, I'm not going troppo then.
lines.talk_shrug_development: Could be, could be not, mate. Ask me again next season.
lines.talk_stings_development: Nah, that's not it, {player}. You've grabbed the wrong end of the snake there.
lines.talk_lands_relationship: Yeah, that's fair enough. I'll have a proper yarn with {name}, gently.
lines.talk_shrug_relationship: Could be, I dunno, mate. Snakes I can read, people take me longer.
lines.talk_stings_relationship: Scrap that, I never said it. And keep it away from {name}, yeah?
lines.talk_lands_confrontation: Yeah, alright, that's fair, I'll take it. Bit stung, but I've had worse stings.
lines.talk_shrug_confrontation: Righto, {player}, heard. Give me a day with it.
lines.talk_stings_confrontation: Right, so that's where we're at. Good to have it in the open, mate.
lines.talk_door_closed: Nah, I'm done with this one, mate. I'll be under a rock somewhere.
lines.arc_cracks: Caught myself telling you lot about the snake house last night instead of telling the scorpion. Didn't even notice I'd switched, mate.
lines.arc_turn: Always reckoned I was better with animals because animals are easier. Starting to think I just never gave people a proper go.
lines.arc_become: You lot are my mob now, mates. People turned out to be worth the conversation after all, and I'm a bit embarrassed it took me forty years.
lines.arc_failed: Ah, people are hard work, mate. I'll stick to the snakes, they don't take it personally.
lines.alt_turn: Spent three days down the Caverns alone and didn't miss anyone, {player}. That should worry me more than it does.
lines.alt_become: I'm mostly down in the dark now, me and the venom. It's quieter, and quiet's easier, mate.
g_roast_after: Still the worst-behaved school group I've ever had, mates, and I'd take every one of you on every tour.
Loud, jumpy, poke everything, all of you, and you're my favourite species.
lines.g_after_wipe_after: Up, everyone, together, check each other for bites. We got rattled, we get up, and nobody's left in the hole.
lines.g_toast_after: To my mob, the first people I ever liked as much as the animals. Took me long enough, mates.
lines.g_crew_after: This is my mob now, permanent. I still love a snake, but I'd come back up for you lot every time.
g_quiet_line_after: Told the whole camp about the shedding scorpion tonight, and they asked questions. Proper questions, mate.
Picked the campfire over the rocks again. Getting to be a habit.
g_loved_after: Cheers, mate, and I believe you. That's new for me.
That's lovely, mate, and I mean it. I'll keep it.

history.open: Don't mind the scorpion, {player}, she's a sweetheart. I kept reptiles at a sanctuary in Queensland for sixteen years. Taipans, death adders, crocs, and a great deal of explaining.

options.reply: That the animal isn't evil, mate. It's frightened, and you're enormous. Every bite I ever took was me being too big in the wrong place.

options.text: Your arms are covered in scars.
options.reply: Professional development, mate, every one of them. Want me to talk you through the map?
Heaps, mate, every day. The snake house at feeding time, quiet and warm. I've built a hut full of jars here to make up for it.

history.open: I go down the Wailing Caverns regularly, {player}. The serpents down there are a lot more than serpents, and they've got strong views about visitors. I'd like to meet whatever's right at the bottom.

options.reply: Because it's the most interesting thing in this whole world, probably. I know exactly how that sounds, mate.

options.text: That sounds like a terrible idea.
options.reply: Oh, it is, absolutely. The Crossroads made me promise never to bring anything up alive again, and I promised them.

history.open: Got bitten by a taipan once, {player}, back home. Inland taipan, most venomous snake on earth, and I nearly died of it. I tell it like a holiday story, and it wasn't one.

options.reply: It was quiet, mostly. Lying on the snake-house floor waiting for the antivenom, thinking the snake was only doing its job. I've never blamed it.
Cheers for that, mate. Me too, most days. It's why I'm not scared of much down here, and why I probably should be.

friend.open: I had a blue heeler back home, {player}, called Biscuit. Went everywhere with me, sat outside the snake house every day. I miss her more than most people, and I'm a bit embarrassed about that.

options.reply: Yeah, you're right. Somebody's looking after her, I reckon, somebody kind. That's the version I keep.
Barked at every snake and never once went near one. Smartest animal I ever met, and I've met heaps.

sworn.open: I've always trusted animals more than people, {player}. You're the first person I'd trust the way I trust a snake I've handled for ten years. That's the biggest compliment I've got, mate.

options.reply: Good, because I don't hand that out, not ever. You're family now.
Don't tell her, but yeah, mate. Even more than the scorpion.

reconciled.open: {name} and I sorted it, properly, and we're good now. Wanted you to hear it from me first.

options.reply: Cheers, mate, I appreciate it. Nobody bit anybody, either.
Me, believe it or not. You learn when to back off from a cornered animal.
